Reader API

The library exposes one typed result to every adapter. Callers receive content, a full outline, provenance, an independent completeness verdict, and a declared coverage mode. The contract is deliberately stable so a command line client and an MCP client cannot invent different meanings for the same read.

Request contract

A normal request asks for full coverage. A token budget may deliberately return a core prefix on section boundaries. That bounded response names every omitted section and gives the exact remaining section count and estimated token cost. This value decision never edits the verifier result.

Python example

result = reader.read(
    "https://example.test/guide",
    budget_tokens=800,
)
assert result.coverage == "core"
assert result.completeness.status == "complete"

The example intentionally demonstrates orthogonal axes. Complete says the source was captured and verified. Core says the returned payload is a declared bounded view of that verified source.

Failure behavior

Retrieval, rendering, extraction, verification, policy, and dependency failures remain typed. A browser challenge returned with a successful HTTP code is still a block. A first page with explicit next-page controls is still incomplete until a recipe follows and verifies every page.
